Fable-Opus-Unit: bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/T005a-ingest-license-cli
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 30

## Goal

Make `ingest` and `license-at-pin` operator stages that admit an application the pipeline has never seen, with no per-app source file, and lift the two hardcoded allowlists that currently gate admission.

Context. The owner outcome is `versionless migrate <app>` running unattended to a coverage report — nobody hand-authors files. Today ingest is one TypeScript module per application: `packages/cli/src/fixture/` holds 34 `*-ingest.ts` files (e.g. `react-papercups-*`, `angular-fuxa-*`), and `packages/cli/src/fixture/legacy-candidate-ingest.ts:63` exports `legacyCandidates` with exactly one entry, while `packages/cli/src/cli.ts:73-81` carries a second hardcoded allowlist. An unseen app cannot be admitted without editing source. That edit is a human intervention inside the run this goal has to prove intervention-free.

Read first, in this order: `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T001-plan-validation.md` (the ruling — sections on acquisition and manual steps), then `packages/cli/src/fixture/ingest.ts` (the shared ingest primitives), then three representative per-app ingest modules of your choosing (one React CRA, one Angular, one that binds a source with a license) to extract the generic shape and the per-app delta, then `packages/cli/src/operator/flows.ts` (`OPERATOR_COMMANDS` at :45; the pattern T004 established for `install`/`build` stages, declared policies with refusing defaults, and the `PipelineRefusal` type in `packages/cli/src/operator/refusals.ts`).

Deliver:

1. An `ingest` operator stage in `packages/cli/src/operator/` that takes an application source (local path at minimum; a pinned git ref if the existing ingest primitives already support it) plus the values the 34 modules vary on, as CLI flags or inferred from the tree — and produces the same ingest record shape the per-app modules produce today. Anything the generic stage cannot infer for a given app is a named `PipelineRefusal` (origin `pipeline`, stage `ingest`), never a guessed default.
2. A `license-at-pin` stage, or a license step inside `ingest` if that is the shape the primitives already have, that records the license observed at the pinned source and refuses (named, exit 2) when it cannot be determined — following the declared-policy-with-refusing-default shape T004 set for the three npm policies.
3. `legacyCandidates` and the `cli.ts:73-81` allowlist stop gating admission. Preserve them if existing tests or evidence read them, but admission must not require an entry. Record which existing behaviours still consult them, if any.
4. Both stages exposed through `runOperatorCommand` with `--json`, exit 2 refusal / 1 defect / 0 proceeded, and wired into `migrate` behind the same declared-flag pattern as `--install`/`--build` (T004 made those opt-in so the exit-0 verify path needs no registry; do the same).
5. Tests: `packages/cli/test/operator-ingest.test.ts` proving that at least one application from the existing 34 ingests through the generic stage to a record equivalent to its hand-written module's record, and that an application missing an inferable value refuses with a named code rather than proceeding.

Do NOT rewrite the 34 per-app ingest modules. This unit is the generic path beside them; retiring them is a later decision, and their committed evidence is sealed. Do NOT touch era-cell provisioning; that is the next unit (T005b).

## File contract

- `packages/cli/src/operator/**`
- `packages/cli/src/fixture/legacy-candidate-ingest.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`
- `packages/cli/test/operator-ingest.test.ts`
- `packages/cli/test/operator-flows.test.ts`
- `evidence/runs/operator-flows/**`

## Forbidden moves

- Do not write anywhere inside `packages/frameworks/react`, `packages/frameworks/angular`, `packages/core/src/migrations`, `packages/core/src/bundlers`, or `packages/core/src/analysis`. Why: those are the five sealed subtrees under freeze `27741d9c`; a write there is freeze motion, which this tranche only authorises once, later, on a separate isolated unit.
- Do not edit or delete any of the 34 existing `packages/cli/src/fixture/*-ingest.ts` modules, or `packages/cli/src/fixture/ingest.ts`. Why: their committed evidence under `evidence/ingests/` is sealed and byte-verified; changing a producer invalidates a receipt.
- Do not invent a second refusal vocabulary. Use `PipelineRefusal` from `packages/cli/src/operator/refusals.ts` and add codes to the census producer if the census test requires it. Why: refusals must stay countable through one surface.
- Do not restate a bounded claim more generally in code, output, comments, or evidence. Why: this repo's coverage claims are deliberately bounded and derivation-guarded.
- Do not run `vp fmt` repo-wide or leave its reformatting in the diff. Why: it touches 249 pre-existing files (the format epoch, a separate later unit).

## Verification

```verify
npm run lint
npm test
npm run trust:verify -- --offline
npm run receipt:verify
git diff --quiet HEAD -- packages/frameworks/react packages/frameworks/angular packages/core/src/migrations packages/core/src/bundlers packages/core/src/analysis && echo FREEZE-INTACT
git diff --quiet HEAD -- packages/cli/src/fixture/ingest.ts && echo INGEST-PRIMITIVES-UNTOUCHED
```

`npm test` takes ~150s; the green baseline after T004 is 2527/2527. `npm run trust:verify` WITHOUT `-- --offline` fails by design.

## Blocked permission

If evidence is missing, the contract conflicts with reality, or you need a file outside the contract, return status "blocked" with the question in open_questions instead of improvising. Specifically block, do not improvise, if: the ingest primitives cannot admit an app without a source edit and closing that gap needs a file outside the contract; a value the 34 modules vary on cannot be inferred and has no honest refusing default; or making this work needs the sealed subtrees.

216	## 4. Human-intervention counting method
217	
218	The gate must not be scored by the thing under test. **A harness outside the command snapshots, spawns the
219	command exactly once, re-snapshots, and writes the record.** T008's Judge re-runs the harness in a clean
220	checkout and compares.
221	
222	### Definition
223	An **intervention** is any act, between invocation and terminal exit, that (a) changes bytes on disk outside
224	the command's own declared write set, (b) supplies an input the command did not obtain itself, or (c) is
225	required for the command to proceed.
226	
227	### Four counters. The gate passes only when all four are zero.
228	
229	**C1 — Worktree mutation outside the declared write set.** Snapshot sha256 for every tracked path in the
230	checkout, the app root, and the lane parent, before and after. The command declares its write set:
231	`--out <lane>`, `--record <file>`, and the `evidence/**` paths it names. Any changed or created path outside
232	that set counts one intervention and is named. Reuse `sha256` from
233	`packages/core/src/receipts/canonicalize.ts`.
234	
235	**C2 — Prompt / stdin reads.** Spawn with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` and `CI=1`. Any stdin read
236	fails by construction. A block with no stdout for longer than the stage budget is a **hang**, which the
237	charter classifies as a defect, not a refusal — score it `defect:hang`, not as an intervention.
238	
239	**C3 — Invocations.** Exactly one process spawn is permitted; the record carries `invocations: 1`. Any second
240	command — including a retry with different flags — counts one intervention per retry. This counter catches
241	spike C's C3 finding literally: `npm ci` exit 1 (`EALLOWREMOTE`) followed by
242	`npm ci --allow-remote all --no-audit --no-fund` was "installed on the second attempt after one operator
243	decision" (`thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json` → `stageLedger.stages[2]`). Under this counter that run scores 1,
244	not 0.
245	
246	**C4 — Authoring-home writes.** Snapshot the eight homes in §2.6 before and after:
247	`fixtures/**`, `packages/cli/src/fixture/**`, `packages/cli/src/witness/**`,
248	`packages/core/src/receipts/witness-*.ts`, `packages/core/src/receipts/capability-coverage.ts`,
249	`packages/core/src/corpus/conformance.ts`, `packages/trust/src/generate.ts`,
250	`packages/cli/src/fixture/legacy-candidate-ingest.ts`, and `.versionless/work/**/*.{mjs,sh}`.
251	Any create or modify counts one intervention per file, named. This is the counter aimed squarely at the
252	silent-manual-residue misfire.
253	
254	### Record
255	Schema `versionless.intervention-count.v1`, written by the harness, containing: `invocations`,
256	`stdinReads`, `mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet[]`, `authoringPathsTouched[]`, `interventionCount` (the sum),
257	`exitCode`, and `terminalClassification` ∈ {`proven`, `refused:<code>`, `defect:<kind>`}. Judge verification =
258	re-run the harness in a clean checkout, compare `interventionCount` and `terminalClassification`.
259	
260	### Explicitly NOT interventions
261	Machine time. The command's own writes into its declared lane / record / evidence paths. Network fetches the
262	command performs under a recorded consent id. A **refusal exit** — that is an outcome the report tallies, and
263	the oracle explicitly admits "names a countable refusal reason" as a passing terminal state.

267	Install policy decisions (remote-tarball allowance; install-script allowance). Adapter admission judgment for

`node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts report:enterprise --offline --verify-only`.

---

## 1. Does Option 1's sequencing survive?

**Yes. The brief was right about the order, and the clarification strengthens it rather than weakening it.**
Do not reorder Workstream 1 and Workstream 2.

The brief ranked "Workstream 1 — end-to-end pipeline automation (~15–25 units)" then "Workstream 2 — the
Angular 13 cell (~25–35 units)", with the note that Workstream 1 is "day-one leverage, no claim risk"
(`docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/notes/owner-decision-brief.md` §5). Under the clarified outcome, coverage
breadth *is* the product, and coverage breadth is per-app-cost-bound: the brief's own §2 says "The cost is
**authoring**: witness journeys/calibration were ~48% of the largest tranche's units". Anything that lowers
per-app cost multiplies every later app. So pipeline-first is not merely defensible, it is now the only
sequencing that makes the coverage half affordable. Option 3 (13-cell first) is worse under the clarification
than it was under the brief.

**Three things do change.**

**(a) The fleet screen is promoted from "day one, item 2" to a Phase-1 input.** The brief put it in §8 as an
immediate next step. Under the clarification it is load-bearing: coverage breadth cannot be planned without
the admission census, and `analyze` costs 0.36 ms/app median (`evidence/spikes/fleet-batch-dryrun/fleet-summary.json`
→ `extrapolation.byStage`). It should be a deliverable of the first Worker slice, not a separate errand.

**(b) The brief's Workstream 1 envelope is not one tranche's worth of work — it is five stages, one of which
(witness industrialization) is on its own larger than the whole envelope.** See §5.

**(c) A stage the brief never names sits between "the command runs" and "the coverage number moves": the
coverage report's own derivation has a hard ceiling in source.** See §3, "The ceiling".

**Against the named misfire.** The misfire is "building a polished staged demo instead of moving coverage."
Option 1's sequencing does not commit that error *provided* Phase 1 is judged by T008 on an app the pipeline
has never handled — never on the fixture corpus. The existing corpus is exactly the trap: 12 apps are already
ingested and staged under `.versionless/work/`, a batch driver already loops them
(`packages/cli/src/fixture/fleet-batch-spike-run.ts:81` — `FLEET` is a hardcoded 12-entry list of
`.versionless/work/*` paths), and it already renders an honesty-guarded summary
(`fleet-batch-spike-run.ts:876,880`). A convincing "one command over the fleet" demo could be assembled from
that in a day and would move coverage by zero. T008's "not on a fixture-corpus app" constraint is the guard
and it must not be relaxed.

---

## 2. What the brief does NOT price

Six items. The first four were named in the task; the last two are additions I found in source.

### 2.1 The zero-manual-steps bar as a *measured* gate
The brief treats "none of that may stay manual" (§2) as a ruling to obey, and prices the automation of each
named stage. It prices no *measurement apparatus*. There is nothing in the repo today that counts
interventions — no schema, no harness, no snapshot/compare. §4 specifies one. Cost: **2–3u**, and it must
exist before T008, not after, or T008 degrades into the judgement call the board created it to avoid.

### 2.2 The coverage report as a first-class emitted artifact
The brief's §6 lists the "honesty-guarded batch summary (spike B) as the operator's daily surface." That is a
*spike record* (`evidence/spikes/fleet-batch-dryrun/fleet-summary.json`, schema
`versionless.spike.fleet-batch-dryrun.fleet-summary.v1`), written by a fixture-scoped driver, outside the
trust manifest, and therefore outside the derivation guard. The oracle's coverage half is "the coverage
report's proven-app count and capability matrix strictly above the sealed baseline" — a claim that only means
something if the report is derivation-guarded and offline-verifiable. Promoting the spike summary to a
guarded artifact is unpriced work. Cost: **4–6u** (§3).

### 2.3 Coverage breadth as the deliverable rather than the 13-cell alone
The brief prices the 13-cell at ~25–35u and says it "Moves ~25 → ~125+ of your Angular fleet." Read carefully:
that is a statement about *addressable* population, not proven apps. Spike A is explicit — "The proving-app
half of the estimate is the part this spike does not de-risk"
(`evidence/spikes/ngcc-1213-feasibility/verdict.json` → `overall.t001EstimateReasoning[3]`) and "Does the
~125-app fleet estimate hold library-by-library? Three libraries were measured. The 5-of-6 prevalence figure
is about the condition, not about these three packages" (`openQuestions[3]`). The cell opens a door; walking
through it 100 times is the deliverable and is priced nowhere. Cost: **16–28u** across two batches (§5).

### 2.4 Sourcing and vendoring the apps to grind
This is the largest unpriced item and it has hard evidence.

- `evidence/ingests/` holds **55** records. Classified by `source.json.result`: **15 `source-bound`**,
  **1 `source-bound-not-admitted`**, **39 with no `source.json` at all** (attempt-only / consumed-failed, e.g.
  `evidence/ingests/react-takenote/consumed-failed.json`). Historical yield from attempt to bound source is
  roughly 29%.
- Acquisition is gated by a hand-authored allowlist: `packages/cli/src/fixture/legacy-candidate-ingest.ts:63`
  `export const legacyCandidates` contains **exactly one entry** (`react-papercups-v1-0-0`), each entry
  carrying `owner`, `repository`, `tag`, `frontendRoot`, `lockFileName`, acquisition byte caps,
  `requiredRevisionWindow`, and a `legacyCell` with install/build commands. `isLegacyCandidateId` refuses
  anything else, and `cli.ts:73-81` carries a second hardcoded fixture allowlist.
- Spike C priced the *pre-migration* stages on one real acquisition: "the cost of the pre-migration stages
  alone was 37 seconds of machine time against about 22 minutes of operator time across four refusals, and
  the run ended with zero builds, zero witness passes and zero new TypeScript lines"
  (`evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json` → `verdict.statement`).

The brief priced authoring. It did not price acquisition, license-at-pin screening, consent recording, or the
~71% attrition before an app is even a candidate.

### 2.5 (Addition) The coverage report's numbers cannot rise without hand-editing TypeScript
Found in source, not in any brief or spike. Four places:

1. `packages/core/src/corpus/conformance.ts:706-707` — the summary is typed with **literal unions**:
   `verticals: 10 | 11 | … | 20;` and `sourceApplications: 3 | 4 | … | 12;`. **At 12 source applications the
   type stops compiling.** That is a hard ceiling on the coverage half of the oracle, in the type system.
2. Same file, lines 719–1010 — `CorpusTransactionState` is a discriminated union of **18 hand-authored
   members**, one per integrated application (`'react-papercups-browser-proof'`,
   `'angular-super-productivity-browser-proof'`, …), each pinning exact `verticals` / `sourceApplications` /
   `receipts` / `resolvedDependencies` counts, with a matching nested derivation at lines ~1600–1900.
   Every newly proven app requires a new union member *and* a new nested branch.
3. `packages/core/src/receipts/capability-coverage.ts` — `buildCapabilityCoverage()` takes **no arguments**;
   `CAPABILITY_INPUTS` lists `provenApps` as string literals. The classification is genuinely derived from the
   proof count (the file's own guarantee, and `verifyCapabilityCoverage` re-derives it), but the *inputs* are
   a hand table. A new proven app is a source edit.
4. `packages/trust/src/generate.ts:372-457` — the canonical receipt inventory is a hardcoded path list.

Consequence: today, "grind an app to proven" ends in a TypeScript edit. If the coverage report is the last
stage of the single command, that edit is a **human intervention inside the gated run**, and T008 can never
pass. This must land before T012/T013 or the grind produces receipts that cannot enter the report.
Cost: **8–12u**.

### 2.6 (Addition) The per-app authoring homes are eight, not two
The brief names witness journeys and per-app receipt modules. The actual per-app surface, from disk:

| Home | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `packages/cli/src/witness/<app>-run.ts` | 13 files, 61–436 lines (`evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json` → `thinWrapperFloor`) |

The last row is the "silent manual residue" misfire in its purest form and belongs in the intervention
counter's watch set (§4).

---

## 3. The coverage report specification

### Ruling: extend the existing derivation-guarded surface. Do not invent a new one.

The surface already exists and already does most of the job. `versionless supported-matrix`
(`packages/cli/src/operator/matrix.ts`) verifies the trust package *before* reading anything
(`matrix.ts:42-51` — "the trust package did not verify; nothing is quotable"), reads the matrix out of
`evidence/trust/current/enterprise-report.json`, renders counted cells per lineage, holdouts with exact
outcome strings, permanent falsification history, declared boundaries with `neverPublishedAs` withheld
(`WITHHELD_BOUNDARY_KEYS`, `matrix.ts:75`), boundary prevalence, and out-of-matrix capability counts — then
passes the whole text through `assertEnterpriseSurfaceHonesty` (`packages/trust/src/enterprise.ts:935`) before
returning it. That guard is what mechanically prevents restating
`witness-passed-on-bounded-anonymous-catalog-surface` as a generic pass: `enterprise.ts:948-962` strips the
exact outcome string from any line naming the application and then rejects any surviving inflected pass verb.

Building a second, unguarded "coverage report" beside this would be the misfire in artifact form.

### Home and wiring

- **Artifact:** `evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json` (canonical, schema
  `versionless.coverage-report.v1`) plus `coverage-report.md` derived from it and byte-compared at verify
  time — the same generated-pair discipline `enterprise-report.{json,md}` already uses ("Both are regenerated
  from the same canonical receipts and compared at verification time, so an edit to either fails verification
  rather than changing a claim", `evidence/trust/current/enterprise-report.md`).
- **Generation:** added to the artifact list in `packages/trust/src/generate.ts:2049` (currently

  covered by `npm run trust:verify -- --offline` and `report:enterprise --offline --verify-only`.
  **If it is not in that list it is not derivation-guarded and the oracle's coverage half is unverifiable.**
- **Render:** must terminate in `assertEnterpriseSurfaceHonesty(text, 'coverage-report')`. Non-negotiable.
- **CLI:** a `coverage-report` entry added to `OPERATOR_COMMANDS`
  (`packages/cli/src/operator/flows.ts:23`), beside `supported-matrix`. No new top-level tool, and
  `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` needs no change — `isOperatorCommand` already routes.

### Required contents (six sections)

1. **Proven-app count vs the sealed baseline.** From `enterprise-report.json.results.supportMatrix.counted` —
   the numbers `supported-matrix` already prints (`angular: 4 counted of 4`, `react: 6 counted of 6`) — with
   the sealed floor "6/6 React + 4/4 Angular derived matrix" quoted and the delta stated. Also carry the
   `demoted` list verbatim; the Angular denominator is 4 and not 5 precisely because
   `angular-realworld-v15-to-v16` was Judge-declined for `applicationFilesChanged=0`, and a report that
   silently re-counted it would be an overclaim.
2. **Capability matrix vs the sealed baseline.** `8 cross-proven / 50 experimental of 58` from
   `capability-coverage.json.summary`, with the delta and the `crossProvenThreshold: 2` restated.
3. **Refusal census.** Every app that ran and did not become proven: the exact emitted string **verbatim**, a
   stable machine `code`, the condition, and `origin: frozen-adapter | pipeline`. Tallied by code. The two
   real strings on record today, from `fleet-summary.json.totals.refusalStrings`:
   - `React plan: this tree declares neither react-scripts nor a Vite configuration, so no frozen React adapter claims it. This flow refuses rather than guessing an origin toolchain.` (emitted at `packages/cli/src/operator/plan.ts:363-365`)
   - `Angular tsconfig migration: the configuration appears to carry comments. This capability rewrites strict JSON only; a JSONC configuration would lose its comments silently, so it is refused instead.`
4. **Run inventory.** Per app: id, pinned revision, license sha256 at pin, consent id, lineage, terminal
   outcome (`proven` | `refused:<code>` | `defect:<kind>`), and **that run's intervention count**. Hard rule:
   *an app with intervention count > 0 may not be recorded as proven.* This is the mechanical link between the
   two oracle halves and it is what stops the coverage number being inflated by quiet hand-help.
5. **Holdouts and permanent falsification history**, quoted verbatim. Already produced by
   `renderSupportedMatrix` (`matrix.ts:137-155`); reuse, do not re-render.
6. **`notEstablished` block.** What the numbers do not say — the pattern every existing artifact already uses
   (`fleet-summary.json.notEstablished`, the spike verdicts, `renderAnalysis`/`renderPlan` in `flows.ts`).

### The ceiling (repeat, because it gates Phase 2)
Sections 1 and 2 read derivations that cannot grow past 12 source applications without a source edit — see
§2.5. Opening that derivation is a prerequisite for T012/T013, not a follow-up.

---

## 4. Human-intervention counting method

The gate must not be scored by the thing under test. **A harness outside the command snapshots, spawns the
command exactly once, re-snapshots, and writes the record.** T008's Judge re-runs the harness in a clean
checkout and compares.

### Definition
An **intervention** is any act, between invocation and terminal exit, that (a) changes bytes on disk outside
the command's own declared write set, (b) supplies an input the command did not obtain itself, or (c) is
required for the command to proceed.

### Four counters. The gate passes only when all four are zero.

**C1 — Worktree mutation outside the declared write set.** Snapshot sha256 for every tracked path in the
checkout, the app root, and the lane parent, before and after. The command declares its write set:
`--out <lane>`, `--record <file>`, and the `evidence/**` paths it names. Any changed or created path outside
that set counts one intervention and is named. Reuse `sha256` from
`packages/core/src/receipts/canonicalize.ts`.

**C2 — Prompt / stdin reads.** Spawn with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` and `CI=1`. Any stdin read
fails by construction. A block with no stdout for longer than the stage budget is a **hang**, which the
charter classifies as a defect, not a refusal — score it `defect:hang`, not as an intervention.

**C3 — Invocations.** Exactly one process spawn is permitted; the record carries `invocations: 1`. Any second
command — including a retry with different flags — counts one intervention per retry. This counter catches
spike C's C3 finding literally: `npm ci` exit 1 (`EALLOWREMOTE`) followed by
`npm ci --allow-remote all --no-audit --no-fund` was "installed on the second attempt after one operator
decision" (`thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json` → `stageLedger.stages[2]`). Under this counter that run scores 1,
not 0.

**C4 — Authoring-home writes.** Snapshot the eight homes in §2.6 before and after:
`fixtures/**`, `packages/cli/src/fixture/**`, `packages/cli/src/witness/**`,
`packages/core/src/receipts/witness-*.ts`, `packages/core/src/receipts/capability-coverage.ts`,
`packages/core/src/corpus/conformance.ts`, `packages/trust/src/generate.ts`,
`packages/cli/src/fixture/legacy-candidate-ingest.ts`, and `.versionless/work/**/*.{mjs,sh}`.
Any create or modify counts one intervention per file, named. This is the counter aimed squarely at the
silent-manual-residue misfire.

### Record
Schema `versionless.intervention-count.v1`, written by the harness, containing: `invocations`,
`stdinReads`, `mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet[]`, `authoringPathsTouched[]`, `interventionCount` (the sum),
`exitCode`, and `terminalClassification` ∈ {`proven`, `refused:<code>`, `defect:<kind>`}. Judge verification =
re-run the harness in a clean checkout, compare `interventionCount` and `terminalClassification`.

### Explicitly NOT interventions
Machine time. The command's own writes into its declared lane / record / evidence paths. Network fetches the
command performs under a recorded consent id. A **refusal exit** — that is an outcome the report tallies, and
the oracle explicitly admits "names a countable refusal reason" as a passing terminal state.

### Explicitly ARE interventions (the historically real ones, all from spike C's `whatRemainsManual`)
Era-cell provisioning ("choosing and obtaining a Node/toolchain era… no remedy available on this host").
Install policy decisions (remote-tarball allowance; install-script allowance). Adapter admission judgment for
trees outside the react-scripts/Vite declaration. The Vite-era configuration and package rewrite. Witness
journey authoring and calibration.

|---|---|---|---|

the clarification introduced (the measured gate, the emitted report, breadth-as-deliverable) or something the
brief explicitly scoped out (acquisition), plus the one ceiling nobody had looked at (§2.5). The brief is not

must be pre-cut into ≤8u sub-packages by the PM at dispatch time rather than discovered mid-run.

## 6. The first Worker slice

44	export type PipelineStage = (typeof PIPELINE_STAGES)[number];
45	
46	export type PipelineRefusal = Readonly<{
47		/** A stable machine identifier a fleet report can tally by. */
48		code: string;
49		/** The emitted string, verbatim. */
50		message: string;
51		/** The stage that was running when the refusal was raised. */
52		stage: PipelineStage;
53		origin: RefusalOrigin;
54	}>;
55	
56	/** A run that reached a terminal outcome without refusing and without failing. */
57	export const EXIT_PROCEEDED = 0;
58	
59	/** A defect: a crash, a hang, or a tree that will not install. Never a refusal. */
60	export const EXIT_DEFECT = 1;
61	
62	/** A named refusal. The run is over, the reason is countable, nothing broke. */
63	export const EXIT_REFUSAL = 2;
64	
65	/**
66	 * The error a refusal travels in.
67	 *
68	 * It stays an `Error` so that a caller which only knows how to catch errors
69	 * still sees the same message it saw before, and it carries the structured
70	 * refusal so that a caller which knows about refusals can count one.
71	 */
72	export class PipelineRefusalError extends Error {
73		readonly refusal: PipelineRefusal;
74	
75		constructor(refusal: PipelineRefusal) {
76			super(refusal.message);
77			this.name = 'PipelineRefusalError';
78			this.refusal = Object.freeze({ ...refusal });
79		}
80	}
81	
82	/** Raise a named refusal. The message must be the emitted string, verbatim. */
83	export function refuse(refusal: PipelineRefusal): never {
84		throw new PipelineRefusalError(refusal);
85	}
86	
87	/** The refusal an error carries, or `null` when the error is a defect. */
88	export function pipelineRefusalOf(error: unknown): PipelineRefusal | null {
89		return error instanceof PipelineRefusalError ? error.refusal : null;
90	}
91	
92	const REFUSAL_NOT_ESTABLISHED: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
93		'A refusal is a named reason this run stopped. It is not a reading of the application: nothing here establishes what would have happened had the refusal not fired.',
94		'`origin: frozen-adapter` says the rule lives in a frozen subtree, not that the frozen subtree raised this particular error object. The emitting file and line are recorded so the attribution can be checked.',
95		'Exit 2 is a refusal and exit 1 is a defect. A crash, a hang, or a tree that will not install is a defect even when it happens inside a stage that can also refuse.',
96	]);
97	
98	/** The JSON body a refused run emits, for `--json` and for `--record`. */
99	export function refusalRecord(
100		flow: string,
101		refusal: PipelineRefusal,
102	): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> {
103		return Object.freeze({
104			flow,
105			outcome: 'refused',
106			exitCode: EXIT_REFUSAL,
107			refusal,
108			notEstablished: REFUSAL_NOT_ESTABLISHED,
109		});
110	}
111	
112	/** The refusal as an operator reads it: the code, the origin, then the string. */
113	export function renderRefusal(refusal: PipelineRefusal): string {
114		return [
115			`refused: ${refusal.code}`,
116			`stage: ${refusal.stage}`,
117			`origin: ${refusal.origin}`,
118			'',
119			refusal.message,
120			'',
121			...REFUSAL_NOT_ESTABLISHED.map((line) => `not established: ${line}`),
122			'',
123		].join('\n');
124	}
